item.title: Said & Checked, Connecticut, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Jim Himes)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “that's sitting in your bank account right now?” Unsettled. GAO reports that as of March 2026 the FAA had obligated $1.8 billion, 20 percent, of the $9 billion systems portion; House Transportation Democrats put spending at about $1 billion of the $12.5 billion as of Nov. 14. No DOT, FAA or GAO figure for spending in mid-November 2026 was found, so the figures point to most of the money being unspent without settling it.

item.title: Said & Checked, Connecticut, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 5 unsettled (Jim Himes)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “That memo has not been shared.” Unsupported. No official account or public record was found on whether the memo has been given to the House Intelligence Committee. The search covered an Associated Press report and web searches on the committee, congressional leaders and the memo.
  • Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “The only information that has come our way was sort of a glancing, not-on-the-agenda discussion in that meeting.” Unsupported. No public statement from the House Intelligence Committee, or any official account, describing what the briefing covered was found. The search covered web searches on the committee and the briefing; briefings of this kind are classified.
  • Jim Himes, U.S. Representative from Connecticut: “This is not a Congress money problem. You pointed out that there was $50 billion sent in the Biden administration and $12.5 billion appropriated that has not been obligated.” Unsettled. GAO reports that as of March 2026 the FAA had obligated $1.8 billion, or 20 percent, of the $9 billion systems portion of the $12.5 billion, so some had been obligated and most had not; no later figure was found. The $12.5 billion was appropriated in July 2025. The $50 billion figure for the previous administration was not confirmed: the FAA's page on the 2021 infrastructure law could not be read directly.
